reason: The hypothesis directly restates the concept of phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) from P18, which already demonstrated ultra-high ductility by fully recrystallizing the soft phase while retaining the hard phase skeleton in a eutectic HEA. The proposed intervention, mechanism, and material system are taken almost verbatim from P18 and earlier work on differential recrystallization (P22, P37). The only new element is a quantitative prediction of simultaneous strength and ductility increases, but this is an obvious expected outcome of the known PSR approach rather than a substantive new idea.
copied_elements: phase-selective recrystallization of soft phase while retaining hard phase skeleton (P18)
differential recrystallization kinetics between soft and hard phases (P22, P37)
back-stress strengthening from heterogeneous microstructure (P6, P7, P32)
enhanced dislocation storage in soft phase (P37)
hard phase constrains deformation and retards crack propagation (P6, P18)
eutectic HEA AlCoCrFeNi2.1 as model system (P1, P2, P3, P16, etc.)
strength-ductility synergy via lamellar architecture (P2, P4, P6)
